[neRok] "misleading pricing" is basically just a fools tax, because it isn't hard to remember the price of your regulars week-to-week[1], or even day-by-day. if you get stung by the fools tax, then that's just Darwinism - and unfortunately for you, you'll eventually be homeless and hungry once capitalism has extracted all it can from you.
[1]: olive oil is the classic example, because if you must buy your particular brand on an exact date, you're gonna pay "full price". but if you know a week or 2 out that you need olive oil and start to watch the specials, you might get what you want within a week or 2 of when you wanted it. and in the 2 to 4 week period when you've run out of olive oil, you'll probably wish that you bought 2x bottles the last time they were on special, so that you can always stay +1 ahead of the curve.
